verdicts.note: Attacked on strength because the district calls it a 'restore' of an eroded levy and 'not a new tax' (S3). It still lifts the regular-levy rate under chapter 84.55 RCW from about $0.396 to up to $0.45 per $1,000 (S1, S3, S4), about 14% higher, for ten years. That is a levy lid lift, which the taxes pole_b names as a cap lift. +2 matches the Lewis/Thurston treatment of the Timberland lid lift. S1, S3 and S4 exist and support the rate figures. local-control was rightly not mapped: the statement for invokes it, but no state mandate or regional authority is involved.

what_it_does matches S1/S2 ($0.45 for 2027 collection plus nine years; the 2036 amount becomes the base). It matches S3 on 'stop the bleed' and keeping services, and on the 12 towns plus unincorporated area, with Pullman, Colton, Rosalia and Uniontown outside the district. cost_line matches S3/S4 ($0.396 to $0.45) and S1/S3 ($14.30 on $275,000; $5.20 per $100,000). pro_summary accurately paraphrases Golden (2,264 programs, 57,173 items, 'preserves local control', balanced budget). The not-a-new-tax and under-$0.50 points are correctly attributed to the district (S3). con_summary accurately states that no statement against was filed, and gives the district's own if-it-fails language (S3).

Attacked toward 2: the levy is about 12% larger ($57M vs $51M) and $0.13 higher than the 2024 estimate (S1, S6). That is still roughly the same level for a three-year replacement, and the district projects the combined school rate to fall from $3.93 to $3.90 (S4, S5). Under the convention, a replacement at about the same level is +1, and that matches Spokane's entry for the same levy. All four citations exist and support the basis.

Levy amounts, $2.10 rate, about $57M total (S1, S4) and the 2024 comparison ($1.97, more than $51M; S6) are accurate. The program list matches S1/S3. The Committee for Great Schools members are named as in S1, and the 'drastic cuts' and 'This is not a new tax' quotes are accurate. The $3.93 to $3.90 projection is correctly attributed to the district (S4, S5). The few-Whitman-voters note matches S8/S9.

Closest call in this set. On this levy line alone the convention points to +2: dollars rise about 78% ($2.3M to $4.1M) and the rate goes from 9 cents to 10-20 cents (S1, S4, S6), which is not 'about the same level'. Upheld at +1 for two reasons. First, it is a replacement of an existing levy, and the district projects the combined school rate it sits in to dip from $3.93 to $3.90 (S4, S5). Second, Spokane County scores the identical measure +1, and splitting the same measure across packages is worse than the borderline call. If Spokane's entry is ever revisited toward +2, this one should move with it.

Rates and amounts ($0.10/$880,000, $0.15/$1.35M, $0.20/$1.9M; about $4.1M total) match S1/S4. The 2024 comparison (9 cents, about $2.3M) matches S6. The purpose list matches S1. The pro_summary quote and fire-alarm, HVAC, roof, camera and door-lock list match the statement for (S1).

Attacked toward 1, since Albion levied the same $20,000 in 2023 (S3, S4). But no Albion levy was on the 2024 or 2025 ballots (S5, S6), so nothing is collected in 2025 or 2026. A YES vote adds a tax that does not exist now, which is the +2 tier. Citations S1, S3, S5 and S6 exist and support this.

$20,000 and $0.459 ($45.90 per $100,000) match S1/S2, and the Corina Anderson attribution and 'Andersen' spelling note match the dossier. Small wording point, not a factual error: the 2023 levy was for 'police, fire and code enforcement' (S4), so 'similar services' would be more exact than 'the same services'.
S3-S6 show no Albion cemetery levy in 2022-2025. This is a new levy purpose and adds a tax, so +2 is right. All citations exist.
$5,000 and $0.114 ($11.40 per $100,000) match S1/S2. The purpose list and statement-for paraphrase are accurate. The 'no Albion cemetery levy in 2022-2025' claim matches S3-S6.
This is the same $30,000 for the same purposes, approved every year 2022-2025 (S3, S4, S7, S8), at a lower estimated rate ($0.53 vs $0.71/$0.80). It is a clear renewal at +1. Citations exist.

$30,000 and about $0.53, with the earlier $0.71 (2025) and $0.80 (2024), match S1, S5 and S6. The 'continue the current level of support' language is the explanatory statement's (S1), correctly attributed, and the no-statement-for/against lines are accurate. One small point: the dossier states $30,000 only for 2024 and 2025 (the 2022-2023 amounts are n/a). 'a $30,000 levy each year since at least 2022' takes the dossier's own summary sentence at face value, which is acceptable.
$13,500 vs $12,000 in 2024 at $0.44 vs $0.47 (S1, S5), passed every year (S3, S7, S8). About the same level, so +1 is right.

Amounts and rates match S1 and S5, the Mayor Dean Marty attribution and paraphrase match S1, and the passed-each-year claim matches S3, S7 and S8 (all at 74% or more). 2023 is supported only by the unnamed but passing town props (S4).

Direction +1 holds: a park levy is on the ballot every year (S6), and the 2025 one passed 59-37 (61.5%, S3), so a park levy is being collected in 2026 and this continues it. The basis wording does need a fix. 'approved each year since at least 2022' is not supported: 82-68 in 2022 (54.7%, S8) and 87-78 in 2024 (52.7%, S7) are below the 60% that excess levies under RCW 84.52.052 need (the MRSC/RCW rule cited in the sibling Oakesdale, Palouse and Rosalia dossiers, and applied to Rosalia's 59.0% in this same scoring file). The prior amount is also unknown, so 'about the same level' cannot be checked.

Two problems. (1) what_it_does says 'Endicott voters have approved a park maintenance levy each year since at least 2022', but the dossier's own margins, 82-68 in 2022 (54.7%) and 87-78 in 2024 (52.7%) (S7, S8), fall short of the 60% an excess levy needs, which the same scoring file applies to Rosalia's 59.0%. Say it has been on the ballot each year, and drop 'approved each year' or make clear that only 2025 (59-37, 61.5%) cleared 60%. (2) con_summary gives '87-78 in 2024' without saying it fell short of 60%, which implies it passed; add that, as the Rosalia entry does. [Applied to scoring/measures.json display text before commit.]
$35,000 vs $30,000 in 2024 at the same estimated $1.14 (S1, S5), passed each year at 65% or more (S3, S7, S8). This is a renewal at about the same level, +1.
Amounts and rates match S1 and S5, and the purpose list matches S1. The Marty paraphrase is accurate, and the approved-each-year claim holds (all named street levies are at 65% or more).
Same $72,000 as 2025 at a lower estimated rate ($2.24 vs $2.50; S3, S4), passed 2023-2025 (S5-S7). This is a renewal, +1. Citations exist.

Amounts and rates match S1/S3/S4, and the purpose list matches the explanatory statement. The 'Street Fund ... does not generate its own revenue' line and the quote are both in Pfaff's statement for (checked against interim measure-7398.txt), so the pro_summary attribution is correct. what_it_does gives that point as 'The town says'; it is really the statement for, but that is not misleading.

Attacked toward 1: Oakesdale levied for public safety in 2023 and 2024 (S2, S3), so this is a recurring purpose. But no Oakesdale levy was on the November 2025 ballot (S4), so on the dossier's evidence nothing is collected in 2026, and a YES vote adds a tax, which is +2, consistent with Albion Prop 1. One caveat on the basis: 'so it does not continue a levy collected in 2026' is firmer than the dossier, which checked only the November 2025 general and says only that 'the sources do not show it continuing'. Soften the wording. The direction stands.

$14,000 and $0.46 match S1. The hardship waiver and not-in-pamphlet points match S1, the 2024 public safety levy at 81.8% (207-46) matches S2, and the no-PDC-committee point matches S7. Optional: the cost line could mention that the two Oakesdale levies together come to about $2.39 per $1,000, compared with the $4.19 special levy collected in 2025 (S5). Not an error.

Same reasoning as Prop 1. Street levies passed in 2024 (S2) and none were on the November 2025 ballot (S4), so a YES vote adds a 2027 tax, which is +2. Soften the basis to say the sources do not show a 2026 collection; the dossier checked only the November 2025 general.
$60,000 and $1.93 match S1. 'Two street levies in 2024 with about 65% yes' matches 64.8% and 66.3% (S2), and the hardship waiver and PDC points are accurate.

Same $55,000 as 2024 (S5), passed in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (S3, S6, S7), with a ballot-title rate ($0.73058) equal to the 2024 figure and an explanatory-statement rate below it. A clear renewal, +1. Citations exist.

The $55,000 and the two conflicting rates ($0.73058 and $0.5912) match S1, S2 and S4. Resolution 2026-08 and the 'great need' wording match S4. 65.4% in 2025 matches 261-138 (S7). The no-volunteers and PDC points are accurate.
Same $50,000 as 2024 (S5), passed in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (S3, S6, S7), with the rate at or below the 2024 figure. A renewal, +1.
$50,000, $0.6641 and $0.53748 match S1, S2 and S4. Resolution 2026-09 matches S4. 65.9% in 2025 matches 263-136 (S7).

Same $50,000 as the 2024 street levy (S5), passed in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (S3, S6, S7), at a rate at or below 2024's. The purpose now names vehicle and equipment purchase as well as street work. That is not enough of a change to make it a new tax, so +1 holds.

pro_summary says 'Palouse voters approved the same levy in 2024 and 2025'. The dossier shows those were the 'Road Oiling and Maintenance Levy' (2024) and the 'Road Oiling Levy' (2025) (S3, S7), while this one is for street improvements plus purchase, repair and maintenance of street vehicles and equipment (S1, S2). Change it to 'a street (road oiling) levy', not 'the same levy'. The 65.8% (260-135) figure is correct. what_it_does ('asked for a street levy') is fine. [Applied to scoring/measures.json display text before commit.]

The 2025 street levy passed at 69.9% (S6), so one is being collected in 2026 and this continues it, at a lower rate than the $1.77 reported for 2024 (S4). +1 holds. Two basis-wording fixes: (a) 'continues Rosalia's annual one-year $50,000 street levy, approved in 2025' implies the 2025 levy was $50,000, but the dossier gives the amount only for the 2024 request (S4), so say 'the street levy approved in 2025' without the amount; (b) the $1.77 comparison is to the 2024 request, which failed (59.0%, S3), so it should not be read as the current rate.

$50,000 at $1.50 matches S1/S2, and the purpose list (including staff wages, plowing and sanding, and grant match) matches the explanatory statement. 69.9% (153-66) in 2025 matches S6, and 59.0% (186-129) in 2024 being short of 60% matches S3 and S8. The no-volunteers and PDC points are accurate.

Tested toward +2, since the amount rises from $80,000 (2024, S4) to $90,000. It does not hold: the ballot title asks that the levy 'be renewed' (S1), voters approved the street levy in 2024 and 2025 (S3, S7), and the estimated rate is lower ($1.89 against $2.00, S4). That is a renewal at about the same level, so +1. All cited sources (S1, S3, S4, S7) exist and support the basis.

what_it_does matches S1/S2 (chip sealing, potholes, manhole covers, sweeping). cost_line matches S1 ($90,000, $1.89) and S4 ($80,000 at $2.00 in 2024). pro_summary accurately attributes 'continued funding' to the town's explanatory statement, and 67.9% in 2025 matches S7. con_summary matches S1/S10.

Tested toward +2: against the 2024 figure ($60,000 at $1.50, S4) the amount is 33% higher and the rate 12% higher. But the ballot title says 'renewed' (S1), and the Gazette reports a 2025 St. John Prop 2 of $80,000 at $1.85 (S5), which is probably the same levy at the same dollar amount for 2026 collection (its purpose is not visible in the story). +1 renewal holds. Citations exist and support the basis.

Figures match S1/S4, and 72.6% matches S7. Minor point that is not a factual error: cost_line compares only to the 2024 $60,000. The dossier also reports a 2025 Prop 2 of $80,000 at $1.85 (S5, purpose unnamed). Leaving that out makes the request look more like an increase than it may be. Optional: add 'a 2025 St. John Proposition 2 was $80,000 at $1.85'.

Tested toward +1: the $50,000 equals the 2024-approved levy collected in 2025 (S7, S10), and the estimated rate is lower ($1.23 against $1.36). But the November 2025 levy drew 58.2%, under the 60% excess-levy threshold (S9, S11), so the dossier shows no Tekoa street levy collected in 2026. A YES re-imposes a lapsed tax rather than continuing one, so +2 fits the convention. The lapse is inferred from the vote share, with no certification found (sources_note says so). S1, S9 and S11 exist and support the basis.

pro_summary calls it 'a $187,600 Transportation Improvement Board sidewalk application'. Per S5, $187,600 is only TIB's share of a $227,600 sidewalk project; the other $40,000 is the match from the street levy fund. Suggested wording: 'including a Transportation Improvement Board sidewalk grant application ($187,600 from TIB, with a $40,000 match from the street levy fund)'. The rest is accurate: Palmer's and Lucki's statements (S1), one council no vote (Thomas, S5), and 58.2% (S9). [Applied to scoring/measures.json display text before commit.]

Tested toward +1: DOR shows an unitemized $65,000 Uniontown special levy for 2025 (S7), and the 2024 library levy covers 2025 and 2026 (S3, S5). But those are park and library levies with a different purpose. No general operations, water/sewer or maintenance levy appears in the 2024 or 2025 results (S3, S6), so this is a new levy and +2 holds. Citations exist.

Matches S1 (about $30,000, $0.64, wages excluded, no explanatory statement) and S4 ($224 on $350,000, unanimous June 10 vote, and Councilman Barry's 'might be a hard sell' quote, attributed accurately to a council member).

Same $75,000 a year as the special levy collected in 2024 and 2025 (S5, S6), at about the same rate ($0.36 against $0.354). The four-year term does not raise the yearly burden. +1 continuation holds. S1, S5 and S6 support the basis.

Resolution 2026-1, the 2027-2030 term and $75,000 match S1/S2. LaCrosse matches S3/S4. $0.354 special and $0.285 regular match S5. $108 on $300,000 is computed from $0.36. 68% (67.7%) in 2022 and 67% (67.3%) in 2025 match S7/S8.

A levy lid lift from $0.63305 (2025, S4) to $1.08 (S1), about 71% higher, is a cap lift (taxes pole_b), so +2. Both citations exist and support it. The lack of a 2026 rate does not weaken the call: 1%-limited regular levies only drift downward in rate.
Matches S1 (rate, purposes, Resolution 26-03, base for chapter 84.55 limits), S3 (Colton), S4 (2025 rate $0.63305) and S1/S2 (hardship waiver). $324 against about $190 is arithmetically correct.

$75,000 equals the 2025 collection (S6), the rate is about the same ($0.31 against $0.295), the levy was approved every year 2023-2025 (S3-S5), and the explanatory statement says 'continue to support' (S1). +1 holds. S1 and S6 support it.
Purposes and youth programs match S1/S2. Approved every year since at least 2023 matches S3-S5. $93 on $300,000 is computed from $0.31. Bailey's quote and Chastain's quote are verbatim from S1/S2.

Tested toward +1, since $140,000 is slightly below the $150,000 collected in 2024 (S8). Rejected: against the most recent published year it is more than four times the $30,000 ($0.31) collected in 2025 (S7). No November 2025 measure appears (S6), so there is no evidence of a 2026 levy at this level, and the ballot title ties the money to 'increased' costs and new equipment (S1). That is not a continuation at about the same level, so +2. Citations S1, S7 and S8 exist.
Matches S1 ($140,000, $1.05, Resolution 2026-04, purposes), S7/S8 ($150,000 in 2024, $30,000 at $0.31 in 2025) and S2 (hardship waiver). $315 on $300,000 is correct.

$75,000 equals the 2024 and 2025 collections (S7, S8), at a slightly lower rate ($0.2506 against $0.290), with yearly approvals 2022-2025 (S3-S6). +1 holds. The separate 2025 splash-pad capital levy (59.9%, S6) is not this measure and does not change the call.
The purpose language, $75,000, $0.2506, the yearly approvals since 2022 and the same amount in 2024/2025 all match S1 and S3-S8. $75 on $300,000 is correct.
$120,000 equals the 2025 collection (S7), at a lower estimated rate ($0.53 against $0.69), with yearly approvals 2022-2025. +1 holds. S1 and S7 support it.
Matches S1 ($120,000, $0.53, purpose) and S7 ($120,000 at $0.69299 in 2025). $159 on $300,000 is correct. Yearly approvals since 2022 match S3-S6.

Tested toward +2 for consistency with Tekoa. The district had no special levy in 2024 (S6) and no November 2025 measure (S4), so a 2026 levy is not shown. Unlike Tekoa, though, no failed vote shows a lapse; the dossier only says 2026 collection 'was not found'. The amount is identical to the last levy ($65,000, S5) at the same rate (about $0.42), so the burden does not rise against the last year levied. +1 holds, but it is the weakest +1 in this set. If 2026 is confirmed to have no levy, +2 would match the Tekoa treatment.
Matches S1 ($65,000, $0.42 or less, purposes), S3 (2024 approval) and S5 ($65,000 collected in 2025). 'Up to about $126' is correct. sources_note correctly says 2026 collection was not found.
$70,000 against $70,531 (2024) and $70,000 (2025) (S7, S8), at a lower estimated rate ($0.35 against $0.45), with yearly approvals since 2022, and the ballot title says 'continued'. +1 holds.
Matches S1, S3-S8. 'About the same amount' for 2024/2025 is correct ($70,531/$70,000). $105 on $300,000 is correct.

Tested toward lower strength: the request falls to $105,000 from $120,000 (2025) and $140,000 (2024) (S7, S8). It is still a YES to continue a tax, which the convention scores +1 (renewal, not a raise). 0 would erase the lean on what remains a levy approval. +1 holds. Citations exist.

Figures match S1/S2/S7/S8, and $246 is correct. Two small points that are not factual errors. (1) what_it_does names the cemeteries 'Garfield and Silver Creek'; the dossier names them 'the district's cemetery (WCCD2) and Silver Creek Cemetery', so 'Garfield' is inferred from the district name. (2) pro_summary attributes the 'has been able to reduce the requested amount this year' quote to Kildew's statement for; the dossier attributes it only to 'the board's statement' [S1][S2]. Both are plausible readings, worth checking against the guide text.

$20,000 is 25% more than the last special levy ($16,000, 2025, S5). There was no special levy in 2024 (S6) and none on the November 2025 ballot (S4), so this is neither a same-level continuation nor a shown current levy, and +2 holds. Caveat on the 'about twice the rate' language: $16,000 at $0.075 implies about $213M of assessed value, and $20,000 at $0.16 implies about $125M. The district's own $0.16 estimate looks high relative to the 2025 base, so the rate comparison overstates the rise. The dollar increase plus the lapse still support +2.
Matches S1/S2 ($20,000, $0.16, one year of maintenance and operation) and S5 ($16,000 at $0.075 in 2025). $48 on $300,000 is computed from the district's estimate. Pro and con match S1.

The ballot title says it 'renews an existing levy that expires in 2026' (S1), at the same $40,000 as 2025 (S6) and 2026 (S8), with $0.37 against $0.38. This is the textbook +1 case. Citations exist and support it.
Matches S1/S2 (Resolution 2026-1, renewal quote, $40,000, $0.37) and S8 (2026 levy about $0.38). '68% to 71%' matches 68.0/70.8/69.5% (S3-S5). $111 on $300,000 is correct.
